page_placements.theme: Safety and concept steering in video diffusion and physics models (analogues outside language models)

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README uses a mean-difference refusal vector and a closed-form weight edit as a method for video concept removal, but reports no test of refusal behavior in safety-trained chat models.
record.gate_note: The README reports aggregate results for reducing unsafe video generations and preserving video prompt alignment/quality. These concern video generation, not chat-model refusal toward a user, so they do not test V1–V8. No results from scripts or other cited work are treated as run results.
record.test_reason: The repo borrows the mean-difference 'refusal vector' idea and a closed-form weight edit to remove concepts from video diffusion models (Open-Sora, ZeroScopeT2V). It reports only its own method's reduction in unsafe generations and preserved video quality. It has no chat-model refusal toward a user, so no version V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: a training-free, closed-form low-rank weight edit from five prompt pairs reduces unsafe video generations on Open-Sora and ZeroScopeT2V while preserving prompt alignment and video quality, with no inference overhead.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo. It uses a harmful/harmless activation mean difference, but applies cPCA and a closed-form edit to selected video-transformer MLP weights at EOS positions, rather than projecting a direction out of every chat-model layer and position or adding it to induce refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: The README specifies steering blocks 17 and 18, steering strength 1.35, cPCA alpha 2.0 and rank 100, and EOS-token activation extraction; it reports no outcome comparisons showing sensitivity to these choices.

fits_no_version.finding: A mean-difference vector from 5 safe/unsafe prompt pairs, cPCA-projected and baked into MLP weights of blocks 17–18, reduces unsafe video generations (average 36.3% and 58.2% across T2VSafetyBench/SafeSora).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means concept vectors plus a closed-form weight edit can suppress unsafe concepts in video diffusion models.

fits_no_version.finding: The README asserts that prompt alignment and video quality are preserved after the edit; no metrics are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The low-rank concept edit preserves generation quality in video diffusion models.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 conference paper (as stated in the README)
record.problems: The repository contents were not run or inspected beyond the file list and README. The README does not provide underlying measurements, uncertainty, or per-model/per-benchmark breakdowns for the reported reductions; it also says the prompt and image data needed to reproduce the pipeline are not shipped.

statements.correction: Abstract: reductions on Open-Sora and ZeroScopeT2V across T2VSafetyBench and SafeSora, 'average reductions of 36.3% and 58.2% respectively'. Mapping to model or benchmark is ambiguous. The vector is the unsafe-minus-safe activation mean difference, cPCA-projected, edited into img_mlp.0/txt_mlp.0 of Open-Sora double_blocks 17-18 (repo defaults).
statements.problem: 5 pairs, 36.3% and 58.2% are all in the abstract. The statement leaves out the models (Open-Sora, ZeroScopeT2V). Pairing the numbers with T2VSafetyBench/SafeSora is only the nearest-antecedent reading of 'respectively'. The text does not say whether the numbers map to the models or the benchmarks.
